title: The physical columns of rule_package_version and the payload a compiled package is served in are not in the sources
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1; FSD P7 A2.7; legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 11 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04
description: The TSD P7 T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval in full and names rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case only as tables of the module, with no field list, no state column and no artifact column. Legacy section 11 names the rule_row fields read through RuleEvaluator and no field of a package version. The story therefore reads a state, a valid-from date, an approver, the generated DRL and a SHA-256 from rule_package_version, and serves the compiled model as a claim-checked artifact, with both shapes flagged in section 11.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 lists decision_log_entry (DF-DEC-001 to 031) and approval (DF-DEC-032 to 053) only; legacy section 11 lists DF-REF-002, 003, 007, 012, 013, 052, 053, 054 and 296 to 298 for rule_row and no rule_package_version field; FSD P7 AC-P7-007-01 fixes the change log content of a version, not its columns.
owner_role: TechX and the P7 solution architect
proposed: Take the rule_package_version columns from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary at implementation and keep the state, valid-from, approver, DRL and checksum as the minimum the promotion and the serving need; confirm the artifact payload with the embedded Drools kit of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON.

title: The rule ID of the same allocation row is ALLOC-014 in the legacy story and ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01 in the FSD
source: Legacy RWB-E1-020 AC1 and AC2; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01, AC-P7-003-01, AC-P7-004-01, AC-P7-005-01 and AC-P7-008-01; Template and Rules R3
description: The legacy story names the ALLOCATION row that sends a MORTGAGE case in BKK to queue MTG-BKK-CO as ALLOC-014, and the ASSIGNMENT row as ASSIGN-007. The module FSD describes the same allocation of the same case and the same version with the row name ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01. Both are data values of package ALLOCATION version ALLOC-2026.11, and no source states which label the workbook carries. The story keeps the legacy IDs in its examples and treats the FSD label as an alternative name of the same row.
evidence: Legacy AC1 reads 'allocation rule "ALLOC-014" matches product group "MORTGAGE", region "BKK" and any exposure band, with target queue "MTG-BKK-CO"'; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01 reads 'given owner "U-7101" by row "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01" of "ALLOC-2026.11" in JOB-03'.
owner_role: P7 business analyst and the reference data administrator
proposed: Load the row once with the rule ID the workbook carries and record the other label as the row description; no code, criterion or record shape changes, because the rule ID is copied from the record as it arrives.

title: How the business date, the queue identifier and the owner identifier travel in the decision record is not in the sources
source: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 12
description: The decision-record library fixes the envelope, the idempotency key and the transaction rule, and legacy section 12 fixes the fields of the CaseAllocated event of the monolith (caseId, queueId, ownerId, ruleId, ruleVersion). Neither source states that the local record carries a business date, nor the field names under which the queue identifier and the owner identifier sit in the actions payload, and this slice needs all three to key one entry per case and business date and to show the queue and owner of an allocation.
evidence: Legacy section 12 lists CaseAllocated (EV-02) with caseId, queueId, ownerId, ruleId and ruleVersion and names no business date; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03 keys the dedupe on the event idempotency key only; TSD P7 T3.1 gives decision_log_entry.actions as jsonb with no shape.
proposed: Carry the business date as a record attribute and the queue and owner identifiers as named members of the actions payload, and fix both in the envelope of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON at its contract review; the ledger keys on the pair either way.

title: The text of MSG-P7-009, the text of the chain-break warning and the field name of the per-entry chain result are not in the sources
source: FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-05 and AC-BG-P7-006-01; TSD P7 T7 NFR-035; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 14
description: The FSD fixes the message ID MSG-P7-009 and the field it names, and fixes a nightly hash-chain check with a same-day report to Compliance, but gives no message text for either. The decision-log read needs a field that carries the result of the chain check per entry, and no source names it. The story reports the ID and the field, uses an RFC 9457 refusal without a fixed text, and shows a warning beside a broken entry.
evidence: FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 reads 'it is refused with message MSG-P7-009 naming "ruleVersion"' and quotes no text; AC-BG-P7-006-01 reads 'Checks the decision log chain / Break reported the same day' and quotes no text; legacy section 14 has no MSG-P7-009 row.
proposed: Approve the two texts with the P7 message catalogue and reuse the approved wording; the ID, the named field and the same-day Compliance report are fixed and do not change.

title: No provided operation of the Ownership Map serves a compiled rule package version to the owning service
source: Ownership Map v1, P7 provided operations (19); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04; FSD P7 A2.7 and A2.8; TSD P7 T5.2
description: DP-04 and ADR-017 make rwb-decision the owner of the rule packages and the owning service the place where they are evaluated, and the owning service therefore has to obtain a compiled version from the registry. The Ownership Map attributes 19 operations to P7 and none of them serves a package artifact; the TSD names only the recommendation, approval and decision-log endpoints. The story assumes the artifact is served on the service base as GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} with a model-owner service identity, and raises the missing row.
evidence: Ownership Map P7 provided operations: /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run, /admin/rule-packages, /admin/rule-packages/change-report, /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, /admin/rule-versions, /approvals, /approvals/{approvalId}, /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, /decision-log, /decision-log/{entryId}, the approve and rollback posts and the approval actions; TSD P7 T-A.1 lists API-P7-001 to 008 with no package artifact path.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the Ownership Map owner
proposed: Add the package-artifact operation to the P7 row of the Ownership Map and to the API Specification at the next version, with the same base, the model-owner identity and the checksum in the answer; no consumer changes if the path is fixed differently.
